newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Europe's Ariane rocket to launch U.S. satellite.
newsitem.headline: Europe's Ariane rocket to launch U.S. satellite.

text.p: Western Europe's 91st Ariane rocket is scheduled to blast off from French Guiana on Tuesday carrying a U.S. direct broadcast satellite, the Arianespace company said.
The ECHOSTAR-2 satellite will be launched aboard an Ariane-4 rocket from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana.
A two-hour "launch window" is to start at 2347 GMT.
The satellite is owned by Colorado-based Echostar Communications Corp. DISH and will provide direct to home video, audio and data transmissions throughout the continental United States.
The 2.8-tonne satellite was built by Lockheed Martin unit Lockheed Martin Astro Space and is designed to operate in space for 10 years.
The satellite was originally to be launched aboard a Chinese Long March rocket, but Echostar switched to Ariane following several Long March failures.
